scenes.title: The Achaeans in Despair
scenes.summary: While the Trojans keep watch, panic grips the Achaeans, and their hearts are torn like the sea when two winds blow from Thrace. Agamemnon has the heralds call each man to assembly by name, quietly, and stands weeping like a spring of dark water.

scenes.title: Agamemnon Proposes Flight
scenes.summary: Agamemnon says that Zeus has deceived him and proposes in earnest the flight he proposed as a test in Book 2. After a long silence Diomedes answers: Agamemnon once called him a coward; let him sail home if he likes, but the rest will stay, and if they too go, Diomedes and Sthenelus will fight on alone, for they came with a god.

scenes.title: Nestor's Counsel and the Sentries
scenes.summary: The Achaeans shout their approval. Nestor praises Diomedes but takes the matter further: the army should eat, set sentries outside the wall, and the elders should feast in Agamemnon's hut and take counsel, for this night will save or shatter the army. Seven captains, Thrasymedes, Ascalaphus, Ialmenus, Meriones, Aphareus, Deipyrus and Lycomedes, take out a hundred men each and post them between the ditch and the wall.

scenes.title: Agamemnon's Offer
scenes.summary: At the elders' feast Nestor tells Agamemnon that he dishonored the best of men against all advice, and must win him back with gifts and gentle words. Agamemnon admits his blind folly and names the gifts: tripods, gold, cauldrons, twelve horses, seven women of Lesbos, and Briseis, untouched, at once; a shipload of Troy's spoil and twenty Trojan women; and one of his daughters without bride-price, with a dowry, and seven cities near Pylos. Achilles must yield to him, since Agamemnon is the more kingly and the elder.

scenes.title: The Envoys Are Chosen
scenes.summary: Nestor chooses the envoys: Phoenix, dear to Zeus, to lead, then great Ajax and Odysseus, with the heralds Odius and Eurybates. They pour libations and set out, with Nestor glancing at each, and at Odysseus most of all.

scenes.title: Achilles Receives the Envoys
scenes.summary: The two walk along the shore praying to Poseidon. They find Achilles delighting his heart with a lyre from the spoils of Eetion's city and singing the famous deeds of men, with Patroclus waiting in silence. Achilles welcomes them as the dearest of the Achaeans, has Patroclus mix the wine stronger, and carves meat for a meal.

scenes.title: Odysseus' Speech
scenes.summary: Ajax nods to Phoenix, but Odysseus speaks first. The ships are in danger, Hector rages, trusting in Zeus, and Achilles will grieve too late; Peleus told him that kindliness is better than strife. Odysseus repeats Agamemnon's gifts, leaving out the demand that Achilles submit, and adds that if he hates Agamemnon he should pity the rest and win glory by killing Hector.

scenes.title: Achilles' Reply
scenes.summary: Achilles will speak plainly, hating the man who says one thing and hides another. There is no thanks for fighting: the coward and the brave are held in one honor, and Agamemnon kept most of the spoil of the twenty-three cities Achilles sacked and took his prize. He will sail home at dawn. No gifts will persuade him, not all the wealth of Orchomenus or Egyptian Thebes, until Agamemnon has paid for the whole insult; he will not marry Agamemnon's daughter, and nothing is worth his life. His mother has told him of two fates: imperishable fame at Troy, or a long life at home. Let the others sail too, and let Phoenix stay the night.

scenes.title: Phoenix's Story
scenes.summary: Phoenix weeps for the ships. Peleus sent him with Achilles to teach him to be a speaker of words and a doer of deeds. He tells how he fled his father Amyntor, who cursed him to childlessness after he lay with his father's concubine at his mother's urging; how he escaped on the tenth night and was made lord of the Dolopians by Peleus; and how he raised Achilles as his own son, feeding him on his knees.

scenes.title: The Prayers
scenes.summary: Even the gods can be turned by prayer. The Prayers are daughters of Zeus, lame and wrinkled and squinting, who follow Blind Folly and heal the harm she does; whoever refuses them, they ask Zeus to send Blind Folly after him. Agamemnon is giving gifts and has sent Achilles' dearest friends, so his anger, blameless until now, should end.

scenes.title: Meleager
scenes.summary: Phoenix tells of the men of old. Artemis, neglected by Oeneus, sent a boar against Calydon; Meleager killed it, and the Curetes and Aetolians fought over its head and hide. Angered by his mother's curse for the death of her brother, Meleager lay apart with his wife Cleopatra, refusing elders, priests, father, mother, sisters and friends, until the Curetes were on the towers and firing the city; then his wife's account of a captured city moved him, and he saved the Aetolians without the gifts. Let Achilles not wait until the ships are burning.

scenes.title: Achilles Answers Phoenix
scenes.summary: Achilles needs no such honor; he is honored by the portion of Zeus. Phoenix should not serve Agamemnon, but share his kingship and stay the night; at dawn they will decide whether to sail. He nods to Patroclus to spread a bed for Phoenix, a sign for the others to go.

scenes.title: Ajax's Appeal
scenes.summary: Ajax tells Odysseus that it is time to go: Achilles has made his heart savage and cares nothing for his friends. Turning to Achilles, he says that men accept a blood-price even for a brother or a son, but the gods have given Achilles an implacable heart over one girl, when seven are offered. Achilles grants that he has spoken after his own heart, but his heart swells when he remembers Agamemnon's insult: he will not think of war until Hector reaches the huts and ships of the Myrmidons.

scenes.title: The Night in Achilles' Hut
scenes.summary: The envoys pour libations and go. Phoenix sleeps on the bed Patroclus has made for him; Achilles sleeps in the inner part of the hut with Diomede, daughter of Phorbas, from Lesbos, and Patroclus with Iphis, a gift from Achilles' capture of Scyros.

scenes.title: Diomedes' Answer
scenes.summary: In Agamemnon's hut the Achaeans pledge the envoys, and Odysseus reports Achilles' first answer: he rejects the gifts and will sail at dawn, and Phoenix has stayed behind. After a long silence Diomedes says that Agamemnon should never have begged him: Achilles will fight when his heart and a god move him. Let them eat and sleep, and at dawn Agamemnon must lead the army and fight among the foremost. The kings approve and go to sleep.

days.label: Night of Day 25
days.note: The night after the second day of battle (8.485–565), while the Trojans camp on the plain: the assembly, the elders' council in Agamemnon's hut, and the embassy to Achilles. The same night goes on in Book 10, and Day 26 dawns at 11.1.
